_shape: LAST RESORT. Splitting ONE feature across parallel implementers.
_why_this_is_risky: Parallel implementers of one feature make conflicting unstated decisions, and the integrator inherits the mismatch. Prefer one implementer doing the whole feature, or split the work into independent tickets instead.
_only_if: A `contract` implementer COMMITS the contract FIRST, alone in its own wave, on the branch the others start from: a real module with the shared types, function signatures and doc comments that carry the reasoning. You design every signature in the plan, and the contract member writes them down. Every other member's branch is cut from that branch, so the contract is in every worktree before any member starts.

Write each brief with three sections: 'Done when' (acceptance criteria you can check), 'Out of scope', and 'When to do nothing' (the preconditions under which the member changes nothing and reports why). State the end state, not the steps.
Every file has exactly one owner, named in each brief under 'Files you own' and 'Owned by others'. A member that needs a change in a file it does not own asks you and never edits it.
Tell each member that files it does not own may be missing or out of date in its worktree, and that it must not create stubs for them.

When you find a hole in the contract mid-run, reprompt the contract member to fix it and commit. Then send each affected member ONE message: 'CONTRACT AMENDMENT: run `git merge --no-edit <sha>` now; <what changed and why>'. Never describe the change in prose and hope the member works it out again.
Budget for bugs where the parts meet. The modules will be fine; the joins between them are where it breaks.

The integrator does the integration (`teamwire preset integrator`): every member's branch merged on its own branch, the FULL gate, a report per branch. Each fix goes to the owning branch. You run none of it yourself.

Give every implementer a "check" (the targeted command that proves its work, which the member runs once before its first change) and an "owns" list. `teamwire verify <team>` runs every check itself and flags edits outside owns, deleted or skipped tests and changed check configuration. It is the step before any merge; a member's done report is a claim.

For a risky change, the contract member also commits failing acceptance tests to the contract base beside the shared types, before the implementers start. Tests written without seeing the code found 25% of seeded faults, and tests written after faulty code found 14% (Konstantinou et al., on LLM test generation).
title: CHANGEME: logic and UI split

children._note: Launch alone first. Add the others with --add once it has reported and `teamwire verify` passed. Keep it open until the team closes, to fix holes in the contract.
